label: Icon itself
summary: Probably gives the house icon of the map icon layer as an object, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name, it hands over the object itself. Vanilla never uses it on this type; the other uses of the name are for other types.

label: House
summary: The dynasty house that this map icon stands for.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the map icon layer, so the parts below it read the house's data. The result has no registered type in the game's documentation.

label: Icon itself
summary: Probably the house icon object itself, for passing it on to another function.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use Self (the object is passed as an argument, like Decision.Self), it is the object itself. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Window itself
summary: Probably gives the house members window as an object, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the house members window.
details: Vanilla runs it when the close button of the window is clicked. It returns nothing.

label: Member list
summary: Probably the list of characters the house members window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of that window. The game's documentation gives no return type; that it is a list of characters rests on the name.

label: Dynasty
summary: Probably the dynasty whose members the window shows.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type; the lines with the same name belong to characters.

label: Window header
summary: The header text of the house members window.
details: Returns text. Vanilla puts it into a text widget of that window.

label: House
summary: Probably the dynasty house whose members the window shows.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type; the lines with the same name belong to characters.

label: Shows dynasty
summary: Probably whether the window lists the members of a whole dynasty.
details: Returns yes or no. The window can show a house or a dynasty (the house window opens it with 'house' or 'dynasty'), which fits the name. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Shows house
summary: Probably whether the window lists the members of a single house.
details: Returns yes or no. The window can show a house or a dynasty (the house window opens it with 'house' or 'dynasty'), which fits the name. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Window itself
summary: Probably the house members window object itself, for passing it on to another function.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use Self. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Template itself
summary: Probably gives the house template as an object, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: House coat of arms
summary: The coat of arms of a bookmark character's house, on the start screen.
details: Vanilla reaches it through a bookmark character's house template and draws it with GetTexture and GetSlot on the bookmark screens, before a game exists.

label: House culture template
summary: The culture template that belongs to a bookmark character's house; the game reads the house coat of arms mask from it.
details: Vanilla reads the house coat of arms mask from it in the shared coat of arms widget, reached through a bookmark character's house template. The game lists no return type.

label: House motto
summary: The motto of a bookmark character's house, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it under the house name in the bookmark screen's house tooltip.

label: House name
summary: The name of a bookmark character's house, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it on the bookmark screen and as the heading of the house tooltip there, reached through the bookmark character's house template.

label: Template itself
summary: Probably the house template object itself, for passing it on to another function.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use Self. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: View itself
summary: Probably gives the dynasty house window as an object, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Members shown
summary: Probably whether the house members window is currently open.
details: Returns yes or no. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Close house window
summary: Closes the dynasty house window.
details: Vanilla runs it when the close button of the window is clicked. It returns nothing.

label: Close members window
summary: Closes the house members window that was opened from the dynasty house window.
details: Vanilla runs it on a click in the dynasty house window. It returns nothing.

label: Current unity stage
summary: The house unity stage that the house is in now.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context and passes it to GetDecisions, to get the decisions of that stage. The game's documentation gives no return type; it is an object for the stage. The game files do not explain what a unity stage is.

label: Decisions of a stage
summary: The list of decisions for a given house unity stage.
details: Vanilla passes the current unity stage and checks whether the list has any items, to show or hide a part of the window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The house unity stage whose decisions are wanted.

label: Shown house
summary: The dynasty house the window is showing.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context, reads the house's dynasty from it and checks its changelog list. The game's documentation gives no return type.

label: Dynasty houses
summary: The list of dynasty houses the window can show.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the window.

label: Dynasty modifiers
summary: The list of dynasty modifiers shown in the house window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list, and shows that list only when it has items. What the items are follows the name.

label: House modifiers
summary: The list of house modifiers shown in the house window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list, and shows that list only when it has items. What the items are follows the name.

label: House relations
summary: The list of house relations shown in the house window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list, shows how many items it has, and fades a part of the window depending on whether the list is empty. What a relation is follows the name.

label: Unity modifiers
summary: The list of house unity modifiers shown in the house window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list, and shows that list only when it has items. What the items are follows the name.

label: Unity stages
summary: The list of house unity stages.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the house window.

label: Legacies
summary: The list of dynasty legacies shown in the house window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list, and compares its size with 10 to switch between two layouts.

label: Sort options
summary: The list of ways the houses can be sorted in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a selection list. Going by its name and by SortHouses, the items are the sort orders.

label: Selected sort
summary: The position of the sort option that is currently selected.
details: Returns a pair of whole numbers. Vanilla uses it as the selected index of the sort list.

label: Top legacy
summary: The dynasty legacy that is shown as the top one in the house window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context for the part that shows that legacy. The game's documentation gives no return type.

label: Has house relations
summary: Probably whether the house has any relations with other houses.
details: Returns yes or no. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it; the window checks the size of GetHouseRelations instead.

label: Has house unity
summary: Whether the house has house unity.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as a visible condition, and to choose a tab shortcut: tab_3 when yes, tab_2 when no. It also appears in a condition together with the unity tab mode. The game files do not explain house unity.

label: On dynasty tab
summary: Whether the dynasty tab of the house window is the open tab.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to show the tab button as pressed and for the alwaystransparent setting of a widget.

label: On relations tab
summary: Whether the house relations tab of the house window is the open tab.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to show the tab button as pressed and as a visible condition.

label: On unity tab
summary: Whether the house unity tab of the house window is the open tab.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to show the tab button as pressed and for the alwaystransparent setting of a widget.

label: Player has unity
summary: Whether the player is affected by house unity.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla combines it with IsPlayersHouse to show a part of the window only for the player's own house when the player is not affected.

label: Is player's house
summary: Whether the house shown is the player's own house.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla combines it with IsPlayerEffectedByHouseUnity.

label: Click a decision
summary: Handles a click on a decision in the house window.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla passes the decision of the clicked row.

label: Open dynasty tab
summary: Switches the house window to its dynasty tab.
details: Vanilla runs it when the dynasty tab button is clicked. It returns nothing.

label: Open relations tab
summary: Switches the house window to its house relations tab.
details: Vanilla runs it when the relations tab button is clicked. It returns nothing.

label: Open unity tab
summary: Switches the house window to its house unity tab.
details: Vanilla runs it when the unity tab button is clicked. It returns nothing.

label: View itself
summary: Probably the dynasty house window object itself, for passing it on to another function.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use Self. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Sort houses
summary: Sorts the list of houses by the option the player picked.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when the selection in the sort list changes.

label: Toggle members window
summary: Opens or closes the members window of the house or of the dynasty.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla calls it with 'house' on one button and 'dynasty' on another, so the text says which members are listed.

label: Legacy itself
summary: Probably gives the dynasty legacy as an object, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Legacy description
summary: The description text of the dynasty legacy.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it in a text widget of the legacy window.

label: Legacy icon
summary: The icon picture of the dynasty legacy.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the legacy window. The game's documentation gives no return type.

label: Legacy name
summary: The name of the dynasty legacy.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it in a text widget of the legacy window.

label: Legacy perks
summary: The list of perks that belong to the dynasty legacy.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the legacy window.

label: Legacy track icon
summary: The track icon of the dynasty legacy.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the legacy window. The game's documentation gives no return type. What a track is is not explained by the game files.

label: Has icon
summary: Probably whether the legacy has an icon.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type; other types use HasIcon to show or hide an icon.

label: Has track icon
summary: Probably whether the legacy has a track icon.
details: Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Legacy itself
summary: Probably the dynasty legacy object itself, for passing it on to another function.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use Self. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Legacy item itself
summary: Probably gives the legacy entry of the list as an object, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Legacy
summary: The dynasty legacy that this list entry stands for.
details: Vanilla reads the legacy's icon and track icon from it. The game's documentation gives no return type.

label: Legacy tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of this legacy entry.
details: Returns text. Vanilla sets it as the tooltip of the entry in the house window.

label: Total perks
summary: Probably how many perks the legacy has in total.
details: Returns a whole number. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Unlocked perks
summary: How many perks of the legacy are unlocked.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla checks whether it is at least 1, at least 2 and at least 3, each to show a part of the window.

label: Is top legacy
summary: Probably whether this entry is the top legacy.
details: Returns yes or no. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Legacy item itself
summary: Probably the legacy entry object itself, for passing it on to another function.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use Self. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Perk itself
summary: Probably gives the dynasty perk as an object, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Perk cost text
summary: The text that states what the perk costs a given character.
details: Returns text. Vanilla puts it in the perk tooltips and passes the player as the argument.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the cost is shown for.

label: Perk cost only
summary: Probably the cost of the perk as text, without the extra wording of GetCostString.
details: Returns text and takes one argument. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it, so what the argument is cannot be shown.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not shown by the game. By analogy with GetCostString it is probably a character.

label: Perk effects text
summary: The text that describes what the perk does for a given character.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it in the perk tooltip, once for the dynasty's head and once for the player.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the effects are described for.
fields.values: a character, for example Dynasty.GetDynast or GetPlayer

label: Perk icon frame
summary: Probably the number of the frame (picture step) of the perk's icon.
details: Returns a whole number. Other types use their GetFrame as a widget's frame setting. Vanilla has no use on this type, so this rests on the name only.

label: Perk name
summary: The name of the dynasty perk, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in effect texts about gaining or losing a dynasty perk ("Gain the ... Dynasty Perk").

label: Perk name, plain
summary: The name of the perk as plain text, without a tooltip attached.
details: Returns text. Vanilla uses it as the heading of the perk tooltip and as text in the legacy window.

label: Perk itself
summary: The dynasty perk itself, for passing it on to another function.
details: Vanilla hands it to other functions: DynastyView.CanSelectPerkDesc, DynastyView.SelectPerk and Dynasty.HasPerk.

label: Confirmation itself
summary: Probably gives the perk confirmation window as an object, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Associated traits
summary: The list of traits that go with the perk being confirmed.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the legacy window. Going by the name and by SelectTrait, the player picks one of them.

label: Perk
summary: Probably the perk that is being confirmed.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type; the lines with the same name belong to other types.

label: Selected trait
summary: The trait the player has picked in the perk confirmation.
details: Vanilla compares its key with a trait's key, to mark which trait is selected. The game's documentation gives no return type.

label: Select trait
summary: Picks a trait in the perk confirmation.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a trait entry is clicked and passes that trait.

label: Confirmation itself
summary: Probably the perk confirmation object itself, for passing it on to another function.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use Self. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Template itself
summary: Probably gives the dynasty template as an object, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Dynasty coat of arms
summary: The coat of arms of a bookmark character's dynasty, on the start screen.
details: Vanilla reaches it through a bookmark character's dynasty template and draws it with GetTexture and GetSlot on the bookmark screens, before a game exists.

label: Dynasty culture template
summary: The culture template that belongs to a bookmark character's dynasty; the game reads the dynasty coat of arms mask, offset and scale from it.
details: Vanilla reads the dynasty coat of arms mask, offset and scale from it in the shared coat of arms widget, reached through a bookmark character's dynasty template. The game lists no return type.

label: Dynasty motto
summary: The motto of a bookmark character's dynasty, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it under the dynasty name in the bookmark screen's dynasty tooltip.

label: Dynasty name
summary: The name of a bookmark character's dynasty, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it on the bookmark screen and as the heading of the dynasty tooltip there, reached through the bookmark character's dynasty template.

label: Template itself
summary: Probably the dynasty template object itself, for passing it on to another function.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use Self. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Tree item itself
summary: Probably gives the dynasty tree entry as an object, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Children shown
summary: Whether the children below this entry in the dynasty tree are currently shown.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to pick the expand or collapse tooltip, the button frame and what is visible.

label: Character
summary: The character this entry in the dynasty tree shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context and reads the character's name and dynasty from it. The game's documentation gives no return type.

label: Child entries
summary: The list of entries below this one in the dynasty tree.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a nested list, and checks whether it has items.

label: Expanded size
summary: Probably the size of this entry's part of the tree when everything below it is expanded.
details: Returns a whole number. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Line end point
summary: The point where the connecting line to this entry ends.
details: Returns a pair of decimal numbers (a position). Vanilla uses it as the end of a line drawn in the tree.

label: Line start point
summary: The point where the connecting line to this entry starts.
details: Returns a pair of decimal numbers (a position). Vanilla uses it as the start of a line drawn in the tree.

label: Tree size
summary: Probably the size of the tree below and including this entry.
details: Returns a whole number. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Has parent
summary: Whether this entry has a parent above it in the dynasty tree.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to show a part of the entry.

label: Founds cadet branch
summary: Whether the entry's character founded a cadet branch (a side branch of the dynasty).
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to show a marker on the entry. The meaning of cadet branch comes from the name.

label: From other dynasty
summary: Whether the entry is from another dynasty.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as a visible condition. Which dynasty it is compared with is not shown by the game files.

label: Is selected
summary: Probably whether this entry's character is the selected one.
details: Returns yes or no. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Is tree root
summary: Whether this entry is the one shown at the top of the tree.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it for the button frame and for a tooltip that says either 'expand the root' or 'set as the root'.

label: Is top parent
summary: Whether this entry is the topmost parent in the tree.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it with a check on whether the character heads the dynasty, as visible conditions of two parts.

label: Tree item itself
summary: Probably the dynasty tree entry object itself, for passing it on to another function.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use Self. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Set up character widget
summary: Prepares the widget that shows the entry's character and says yes or no.
details: Vanilla calls it in a visible condition and passes the widget itself, so the call both sets it up and decides whether it is shown. What exactly it prepares is not shown by the game's files.

label: Set up top widget
summary: Prepares the widget for the top of the tree and says yes or no.
details: Vanilla calls it in a visible condition and passes the widget itself, so the call both sets it up and decides whether it is shown. What exactly it prepares is not shown by the game's files.

label: Toggle children
summary: Shows the children of this entry if they are hidden, and hides them if they are shown.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on a click in the dynasty tree window.

label: Toggle parents
summary: Shows the parent entries of this entry if they are hidden, and hides them if they are shown.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on clicks in the dynasty tree.

label: Tree window itself
summary: Probably gives the dynasty tree window as an object, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Close tree window
summary: Closes the dynasty tree window.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on clicks of the window's close controls.

label: Dynasty
summary: The dynasty whose tree the window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context, and compares it with a character's dynasty to find the founder of the dynasty. The game's documentation gives no return type.

label: Dynasty houses
summary: Probably the list of houses of the dynasty shown in the tree window.
details: Going by its name and by the same name on a dynasty in vanilla texts, where the list size is the number of houses. Vanilla has no use on this type itself.

label: Dynasty trees
summary: The list of trees the window draws, one entry per tree.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the main list. Each item is a DynastyTreeItem, going by the other functions of this window.

label: Modifiers
summary: Probably the list of modifiers shown for the dynasty.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type; the lines with the same name belong to schemes.

label: Show 'go to me'
summary: Whether the button that moves the tree view to the viewer's own entry is shown.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the visible condition of that part. The wording 'go to me' follows the name PanToMe.

label: Go to dynast
summary: Moves the tree view to the dynast (the current head of the dynasty).
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on a button click. What 'dynast' means comes from the name.

label: Go to me
summary: Moves the tree view to the viewer's own entry.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on a button click. That "me" is the player rests on the name.

label: Tree window itself
summary: Probably the dynasty tree window object itself, for passing it on to another function.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use Self. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Legacy window itself
summary: Probably gives the dynasty legacy window as an object, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Can pick perk
summary: Whether a given perk can be picked now.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to enable the perk button and to show one of two states of it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a dynasty perk, for example DynastyPerk.Self

label: Perk pick text
summary: The text about whether a given perk can be picked.
details: Returns text. Vanilla puts it in the perk tooltips, before the cost text. Going by its name it belongs to CanSelectPerk.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a dynasty perk, for example DynastyPerk.Self

label: Close legacy window
summary: Closes the dynasty legacy window.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on the window's close button.

label: Dynasty
summary: The dynasty the legacy window is about.
details: The game's documentation says it returns a dynasty. Vanilla uses it as the data context of the window, so the parts inside read that dynasty.

label: Legacies
summary: The list of dynasty legacies shown in the legacy window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list, and compares its size with 7 to switch between two layouts.

label: Perk progress cost
summary: Probably the cost of a given perk, as a decimal number.
details: Returns a number with decimals and takes one argument. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it, so what the argument is cannot be shown.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not shown by the game. Probably the perk.

label: Unlocked perks
summary: How many perks the dynasty has unlocked in total.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla shows it after the word 'Legacies:' in a button text.

label: Unlocked in track
summary: Probably how many perks are unlocked in a given track (group of legacies).
details: Returns a whole number and takes one argument. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not shown by the game. Probably the track.

label: Is next perk
summary: Whether a given perk is the next one that can be unlocked.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla combines it with a check that the dynasty's head is the local player.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a dynasty perk, for example DynastyPerk.Self

label: Pick perk
summary: Picks a given perk in the legacy window.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a perk is clicked. What the click does next is not shown by the game files.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a dynasty perk, for example DynastyPerk.Self

label: Legacy window itself
summary: Probably the dynasty legacy window object itself, for passing it on to another function.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use Self. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Toggle members window
summary: Probably opens or closes a members window.
details: Going by its name and by the same function on the house window, which takes 'house' or 'dynasty'. Here the game's documentation lists no argument. Vanilla does not use it on this type.

label: Window itself
summary: Probably gives the emitter node window as an object, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type. It looks like a tool window for effects (emitters) rather than one of the normal game screens.

label: Add user data
summary: Probably adds a piece of user data to the emitter node.
details: Returns nothing and takes one argument. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Node title color
summary: Probably the color of the node's title.
details: Returns a color of four numbers. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Another node isolated
summary: Probably whether some other emitter node is currently isolated.
details: Returns yes or no. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Is isolated
summary: Probably whether this emitter node is isolated.
details: Returns yes or no. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Is visually on
summary: Probably whether this emitter node is switched on in the display.
details: Returns yes or no. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Window itself
summary: Probably the emitter node window object itself, for passing it on to another function.
details: Going by its name and by how other types use Self. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Isolate exclusively
summary: Probably switches the isolation of this emitter node, so that it is the only isolated one.
details: Returns nothing. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Isolate additionally
summary: Probably switches the isolation of this emitter node, in addition to others that are isolated.
details: Returns nothing. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Toggle visible on
summary: Probably switches the emitter node on or off in the display.
details: Returns nothing. Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it.

label: Current page
summary: Gives access to the encyclopedia page that is currently open.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the encyclopedia window, so the parts inside read the open page. The game's documentation gives no return type.

label: All pages
summary: Gives access to the list of encyclopedia pages.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the encyclopedia window.

label: Encyclopedia itself
summary: Probably gives the encyclopedia as an object, so it can be handed to another function.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla has no use on this type.

label: Can go back
summary: Whether the encyclopedia can step back in its history.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to enable the back button.

label: Can go forward
summary: Whether the encyclopedia can step forward in its history.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to enable the forward button.

label: Go back
summary: Steps back in the encyclopedia's history.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on a click of the back button.

label: Go forward
summary: Steps forward in the encyclopedia's history.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on a click of the forward button.

label: All page
summary: The encyclopedia page that lists everything.
details: Vanilla compares it with the current page to show the matching tab as pressed. The game's documentation gives no return type; 'lists everything' follows the name.

label: Current page
summary: The encyclopedia page that is currently open.
details: Vanilla compares it with the all page or with a list entry's page, to mark that entry as pressed or to hide parts. The game's documentation gives no return type.

label: Pages
summary: Probably the list of encyclopedia pages.
details: Going by its name only. The game's texts and GUI files never use it; the window uses AccessPages for this.

label: Viewed entries
summary: The list of encyclopedia entries the player has viewed.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the encyclopedia window. That it is the viewing history follows the name.

label: Hide encyclopedia
summary: Closes the encyclopedia window.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it on clicks of the window's close controls.

label: Is shown
summary: Probably whether the encyclopedia is currently open.
details: Returns yes or no. Going by its name only; the lines with the same name belong to other types. Vanilla has no use on this type.
